label: prf:jet-tower-convergence
title: Proof of jet tower convergence
html:
Proof. Proof of jet tower convergence

Proof. The geometric series \sum_{k \geq 0} \hbar_q^{2k} converges with sum (1 - \hbar_q^{2})^{-1} because \hbar_q^2 \in (0, 1) (indeed \hbar_q^2 \approx 0.00982 at q_0 \approx 1.11). Absolute convergence follows from the comparison \sum_{n \geq 1} \hbar_q^{2n} |\Delta^{(n)}| \leq \Delta_{\max} \sum_{n \geq 1} \hbar_q^{2n} = \Delta_{\max} \cdot \hbar_q^2 / (1 - \hbar_q^2). The tail bound factors the first skipped term:

  \bigl\lvert \sum_{n > N} \hbar_q^{2n}\,\Delta^{(n)} \bigr\rvert
  \leq \Delta_{\max} \cdot \hbar_q^{2(N+1)}
   \sum_{k \geq 0} \hbar_q^{2k}
  = \Delta_{\max} \cdot \frac{\hbar_q^{2(N+1)}}{1 - \hbar_q^{2}}.

Multiplying by E_0 and solving E_0 \cdot \Delta_{\max} \cdot \hbar_q^{2(N+1)} / (1 - \hbar_q^2) \leq \varepsilon_B for N gives the stated count. \square
